_comment: THE FLAGSHIP: 'How do you represent data-dependent paths on chip?' — a head-to-head, in SIMULATION, between control-on-a-CPU (Tenstorrent's answer: 5 baby RISC-V CPUs per Tensix tile) and control-as-dataflow (our answer: a closed set of 5 spatial mechanisms, PROVEN complete + bit-identical to a reference VM). Every number here is simulated with a stated provenance; nothing is measured on silicon and nothing is Tenstorrent's own power (ttsim reports cycles, not watts — see grounding.ttsim). The two power/cycle figures are OUR Sky130 signoff fabric (control-as-dataflow) vs a RISC-V soft-core (the CPU class Tenstorrent runs control on). This is the architectural gap, honestly labeled.
question: How do you represent data-dependent paths (runtime-decided branches, data-dependent loop bounds, opcode dispatch) on a spatial chip?

control_on_a_cpu.who: Tenstorrent (and every CGRA that bolts scalar cores onto tiles)
control_on_a_cpu.how: 5 baby RISC-V CPUs per Tensix tile fetch-decode-execute the branch/loop; control flow is a von Neumann program counter, not part of the spatial fabric
control_on_a_cpu.source: docs.tenstorrent.com — Tensix architecture (2 data-movement + unpack/math/pack baby RISC-V cores per tile)

control_as_dataflow.how: the compiler turns control-dependence into DATA-dependence and routes it spatially; every language construct compiles into ONE of a closed set of FIVE spatial mechanisms, so control never touches a program counter

completeness_certificate._what: The claim 'ANY program's control routes as dataflow' is not asserted — it is machine-checked. These locks are green in-tree.
completeness_certificate.wprog_completeness_lock: every major LOGOS construct (branch, while, for, list, tuple, call, division, range-loop, float, text, set, recursion) runs on the fabric bit-exactly vs the VM by one of the 5 mechanisms; a regression → RED, a silent new gap → RED
completeness_certificate.wprog_op_reachability_lock: a FINITE TOTAL partition over ALL 115 ISA ops — nothing unclassified
completeness_certificate.universal_completeness_lock: the whole-program composition census on top of op-closure

head_to_head_in_simulation._what: The SAME data-dependent decision over the same input ranges, done two ways, both in simulation and both measured the same way — a signoff-clean Sky130 netlist simulated at gate level at its own signoff clock, VCD → OpenSTA report_power. Control-as-dataflow is OUR decision fabric (decision_hft_realbist). The CPU baseline is OUR routable scalar LOGOS core running the decision from its boot ROM (soft_core_realbist): a single-issue fetch-decode-execute CPU, the class of core a Tensix tile runs control on. This is the architectural power/latency/energy gap of routing control vs running it on a CPU.
head_to_head_in_simulation.workload: realistic data-dependent decisions — a decision kernel over market inputs; over 4000 cycles of gate-level simulation it decided buy 523 / sell 833 / risk-blocked 419 / no-trade 2225, changing its decision on 2266 of them — counted on the RTL, whose signature over the same window the gate run reproduces (92de)

control_as_dataflow.impl: decision fabric (if-converted routed select DAG), OUR design

control_on_a_cpu.impl: the routable scalar LOGOS core running the same decision over the same input ranges (soft_core_realbist), OUR design

the_gap.reading: routing a data-dependent decision as spatial dataflow resolves it in ONE clock edge, 10.8 ns at the fabric's signoff clock, against 105.26 cycles, 2,578.9 ns at the CPU's (105x FEWER cycles, ~239x LOWER LATENCY), and — because energy = power x time — burns ~1,363-1,896x LESS ENERGY per data-dependent decision. Power is each block's at its own signoff clock (3.31 mW for the fabric at 10.8 ns, 18.9 mW for the CPU at 24.5 ns): a faster fabric draws more power for more decisions a second, so their ratio is not the claim. Latency is the trading axis and energy/decision the inference-economics one (energy/token). Tenstorrent runs control on 5 such CPUs per tile.

ttsim._what: We are not hand-waving about Tenstorrent — LOGOS-auto-generated kernels (including data-dependent control) run on the Tensix under Tenstorrent's OWN cycle-accurate simulator (ttsim), bit-exact vs the VM. ttsim reports cycles, not watts, so the power figures above are our Sky130 fabric, not ttsim.

measured_data_dependent_control_on_the_b._what: MEASURED on ttsim (virtual Wormhole b0): a maximally data-dependent-control kernel — collatz step-count, an even/odd BRANCH whose predicate is the running data, inside a loop whose bound IS the data — run on a single Tensix baby RISC-V (Data Movement core, the exact core Tenstorrent runs control on). Inputs are runtime args (get_arg_val) so the trajectory, branch sequence, and iteration count cannot be compile-folded. The step count is the bit-exact check vs the reference; baby_riscv_cycles is the control cost measured by the baby core's own wall-clock register (0xFFB121F0). This is the concrete price of 'control on a CPU' on Tenstorrent's own silicon model — vs our decision fabric's ONE spatial cycle per decision.
measured_data_dependent_control_on_the_b.core: Tensix Data Movement RISCV_0 (a baby RISC-V CPU)
measured_data_dependent_control_on_the_b.reading: Every step count is bit-exact — data-dependent control runs correctly on the Tensix baby CPU. And the baby core spends ~5.6-7 of its OWN cycles per data-dependent decision doing the fetch-decode-branch — control it cannot avoid because it is a von Neumann CPU. Our decision fabric routes the same decision in 1 spatial cycle.

sota_positioning._what: Who else answers the data-dependent-control-on-chip question, and how we are state of the art on it.
sota_positioning.tileloom_osdi_2026: tile/tensor kernels only (MLIR, Triton-style); matches vendor libs on GEMM/FlashAttention/Mamba — NO data-dependent control
sota_positioning.dam_olukotun_isca_2024: a dataflow abstract machine — a MODEL/simulator (CSP-with-time), not a compiler + silicon + completeness proof
sota_positioning.tenstorrent: control on baby RISC-V CPUs (von Neumann) — the very thing this artifact beats by 105x in cycles and ~1,363x in energy per decision, in simulation
sota_positioning.logos_claim: the only stack that (a) proves ANY program's control routes as spatial dataflow (5-mechanism closed set, machine-checked), (b) is bit-identical to a reference VM, and (c) carries a VCD-measured control-fabric power number. That triple is the SOTA on data-dependent control.

honesty.no_silicon: no number here is measured on a physical chip
honesty.power_is_our_fabric_not_ttsim: the 3.31 mW fabric and 18.9 mW CPU figures are both switching measured by gate-level simulation of a signoff-clean Sky130 netlist of ours, each at its own signoff clock, deciding over the same input ranges; neither is ttsim (Tenstorrent's sim gives cycles only)
honesty.measured_hardware_next: a real card / Tenstorrent Cloud (tt-smi telemetry) would add the on-silicon layer; the completeness proof and the control-fabric power gap do not depend on it
